title: Oil, propane or electric heat, plus AC? A national model says 95 to 100 percent of homes save.

scenes.purpose: Land the figure first: the share of oil, propane and electric homes with AC that the model says save.

visual.description: One stat tile centred in the portrait frame; the figure 95%–100% lands on "95" and holds while the sentence names the homes it covers.

chart.title: Oil, propane or electric
chart.note: Homes that already have air conditioning; a modelled estimate, not measured bills.

scenes.direction: Cold open; the tile lands on "95" and holds to the end of the sentence.
scenes.narration: 95 to 100 percent: the share of homes heating mainly with oil, propane or electricity, and already running air conditioning, that a national study estimates would pay lower bills with a heat pump.

scenes.purpose: Turn the figure into the question the short answers.

visual.description: Dark field; one title line types on: what the figure is, and what it is not.
onScreenText: What it is, and is not

scenes.direction: Title types on with the sentence; hold a beat.
scenes.narration: The Commission has looked at what that figure is, and what it is not.

scenes.purpose: Say plainly that the figure is modelled, not metered.

visual.description: Three short lines build down the frame as the sentence moves: it is a model, the bills were simulated, nobody's meter was read.

scenes.direction: Lines on "model", "simulated" and "meter"; hold on the last.
scenes.narration: It is a model: the study simulated the bills of such homes across the country, so the figure is an estimate of what bills would be, not a reading from anyone's meter.

scenes.purpose: Pair the share with the median saving, both for the same homes, both moving with efficiency.

visual.description: Two stat tiles stacked in the portrait frame, reused from the main video: the share of homes with lower bills above, the median yearly saving below; the dollar tile lands on "$300".

chart.title: Oil, propane or electric
chart.note: Modelled estimate across heat pump efficiency levels, not measured bills; homes with air conditioning only.

scenes.direction: Top tile already in place from the hook; the saving tile lands on "$300"; hold a beat.
scenes.narration: The range moves with the heat pump's efficiency, and so does the saving: the median it estimated was $300 to $650 a year, for those same homes and no others.

scenes.purpose: Show the AC condition doing the work: the same fuels without it fall to 73 to 86 percent.

visual.description: Two horizontal bars, with AC above, without AC below; the lower bar draws on "only" and stops visibly short of the upper one.

chart.title: Share with lower bills
chart.note: Each bar is drawn at the low end of its modelled range; same fuels, same model.

scenes.direction: Upper bar in place at the cut; lower bar draws on "only"; hold after the sentence.
scenes.narration: The air conditioning is not a detail: in the same model, homes on those fuels without it do worse, with only 73 to 86 percent coming out ahead.

scenes.purpose: Leave the viewer with the Commission's note on models and the pointer to the full inquiry.

visual.description: Two lines, one per sentence: the note on what a model is exact about, then the pointer to the full inquiry.

scenes.direction: First line with s06, second with s07; hold to the end.
scenes.narration: A model, the Commission notes, is exact about what it assumes. Whether metered homes in Minnesota and New England agree with the model, and whether oil holds the pattern, is the subject of the full inquiry, linked in the description below.
